title: Market explained
description: SEBI has introduced a new way to decide the closing price for certain stocks. This is called the "Closing Auction Session" (CAS) and started on August 3, 2026.

faq.a: These are generally large, liquid stocks that meet certain criteria set by SEBI, allowing investors to trade derivative contracts (Futures and Options) on them in addition to buying and selling the actual shares.

faq.q: Do I need to do anything as a regular investor?
faq.a: For most long-term investors, no direct action is needed. However, understanding how closing prices are determined can help you better interpret daily market movements and portfolio valuations. If you are an intraday trader, be mindful of the earlier square-off times for F&O stocks.

faq.q: Will this affect my mutual fund investments?
faq.a: Yes, indirectly. The Net Asset Value (NAV) of equity mutual funds is calculated using the closing prices of the underlying stocks they hold. A more accurate and stable closing price for F&O stocks will contribute to a more reliable NAV calculation.

faq.q: Why did SEBI make this change?
faq.a: SEBI introduced CAS to improve price discovery, reduce price manipulation at market close, and bring Indian market practices in line with global standards. Large orders placed in the final minutes could sometimes disproportionately affect closing prices, and CAS aims to mitigate this.
